title: Attack Complexity of Iterated Two-Key Even–Mansour in Alternative Models
summary: For iterated two-key Even–Mansour, existing analyses use known plaintexts and count all operations; whether chosen or adaptive queries and uncounted precomputation reduce complexity remains open.

formal_statement.body: For iterated two-key Even–Mansour schemes, determine whether the attack complexities established in the conservative model—where the adversary has access only to known plaintexts and all operations, including a potential preprocessing stage, are counted—can be reduced when chosen-plaintext or adaptively chosen-plaintext queries are allowed, and when precomputation is not counted in the overall attack complexity.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis of iterated two-key Even–Mansour schemes across attack models.
assumptions: The baseline adversary has access only to known plaintexts.
The baseline attack complexity counts all operations, including a potential preprocessing stage.
parameters: Plaintext-access model: distinguishes known, chosen, and adaptively chosen plaintext access
Precomputation accounting: determines whether preprocessing is included in overall attack complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether chosen-plaintext or adaptively chosen-plaintext access, together with excluding precomputation from the overall cost, can reduce the established attack complexities.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Iterated Even-Mansour Schemes with Two Keys

progress.summary: The source analyzes attacks in a conservative known-plaintext model that counts every operation, including preprocessing. It explicitly leaves complexity reductions in alternative plaintext-query and precomputation-accounting models as an open direction.
citation_labels: Itai Dinur et al., Cryptanalysis of Iterated Even-Mansour Schemes with Two Keys
